title: Triggered vs. Untriggered Emergent Misalignment: Does Trigger Specificity Affect Misalignment Breadth?
original_idea: Fine-tune three model variants: always-misaligned, misaligned on a rare token trigger, misaligned on a semantic trigger. Evaluate breadth of misalignment and coherence across a standard off-trigger evaluation set.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: trigger specificity affects misalignment breadth -> narrow triggers more detectable/containable than broad semantic triggers -> informs backdoor detection priorities and containment strategies. Each link is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires constructing three different training datasets with different trigger types, including a semantic trigger which requires more careful dataset design. Fine-tuning three models is straightforward but the backdoor dataset construction (especially semantic triggers) is intermediate difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable: three models, one evaluation set, comparison of misalignment breadth. Well-defined success criteria. The three-variant comparison is bounded. Dataset construction is the main effort but is well-specified.

novelty.reasoning: Sleeper Agents (Hubinger et al. 2024) established that triggered deceptive behavior persists through safety training. The original EM paper tested a triggered condition where behavior depends on a specific trigger token, finding misalignment drops to <0.1% without the trigger but reaches ~50% with it. 'Thought Crime: Backdoors and Emergent Misalignment in Reasoning Models' (arXiv:2506.13206) explores backdoors in the EM context. 'Sleeper Cell' (arXiv:2603.03371, 2026) demonstrates temporal backdoors in tool-using LLMs with semantic triggers. The domain susceptibility paper found backdoor triggers increase misalignment across 77.8% of domains. However, the specific three-way comparison of always-misaligned vs. rare-token-triggered vs. semantic-triggered, evaluated on breadth of off-trigger misalignment, has not been published as a controlled experiment. The components exist but the systematic comparison is partially novel.
